status: drafted via multi-agent workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: Tobit is a tightly-plotted 14-chapter novella and, unlike Leviticus/Deuteronomy, has no thin-narrative/law-heavy stretch — every block of teaching content (Tobit's ch.4 farewell instructions on almsgiving/marriage/wages, his ch.13 hymn, Raphael's ch.12 discourse on prayer/fasting/alms) is delivered as personally-embodied speech folded into that character's own tier rather than a standalone role:"law" tier, so all 7 scribe tiers here are person-type. REAL NAMING COLLISION found and kept separate per the project's collision rule: two different men named Gabael appear — Tobit's own distant ancestor ("son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael," Tobit 1:1) and the unrelated kinsman-trustee Gabael of Rages who holds the ten talents (Tobit 1:14, "brother of Gabrias") — the ancestor is never referenced again and is logged only in genealogyLists, while the trustee is the submanager built into Tobias's tier. Also flagged, not merged: Raphael's assumed human identity "Azarias, son of Ananias the great" (Tobit 5:12) is the angel's own disguise-name within the story, not a real second genealogy for Raphael — his true nature (angelic, no human parentage) is stated directly in Tobit 12:15. A real doctrinal-content note worth flagging for future NT/angelology-adjacent work: Raphael's self-disclosure in 12:15 ("I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints") is the only place in the indexed content so far that names a specific angelic count/office this explicitly — treat as this book's own textual claim, not asserted as cross-book doctrine. This book has no equivalent in the standard 66-book KJV canon (it's part of the wider deuterocanon shared across Catholic/Orthodox/Ethiopian traditions, not a uniquely Ethiopian composition) — drafted fresh with no KJV Character Index counterpart to check against, per the task instructions.

characters.name: Tobit

genealogy.father: Tobiel (Tobit 1:1, unindexed — orphaned young per 1:8, not itself tracked as a character)

verses.note: Opens the book narrating his own five-generation lineage (son of Tobiel, of the tribe of Nephthali).
Introduces himself as walking in truth and justice, giving many alms to his brethren in Nineve.
Alone among his apostate tribe, keeps faithfully tithing and sacrificing at Jerusalem, following his grandmother Debora's instruction after being orphaned.
Defies king Sennacherib by secretly burying the Israelites he slew, at real risk to his own life.
At his Pentecost feast, sends Tobias to fetch a poor kinsman, then leaves his own meal untouched to bury a murdered Israelite found in the marketplace.
Blinded when sparrow dung falls into his eyes while sleeping by his courtyard wall after the burial.
In his grief and blindness, prays for God to let him die rather than continue enduring false reproach.
Gives Tobias his full farewell instructions — honor his mother, give alms generously, marry within his own kindred, pay wages promptly — and reveals the ten talents left in trust with Gabael.
His sight is restored when Tobias applies the fish's gall to his eyes; he weeps and blesses God on seeing his son again.
In old age gives his final testament to Tobias, urging almsgiving and departure from Nineve before its foretold destruction, then dies at 158.

funFacts: Narrates his own story in the first person for the first three chapters before the text shifts to third person.
His dying hymn of praise becomes the whole of Tobit chapter 13.

characters.name: Anna

verses.note: Tobit marries her, described as of his own kindred; she bears him Tobias.
When all Tobit's goods are seized, only she and Tobias are left to him.
Takes up weaving work to support the household; brings home a kid given as a wage bonus, which Tobit accuses her of stealing — she sharply rebukes him, 'Where are thine alms and thy righteous deeds?'
Weeps and protests when Tobias is sent on the journey to Media, calling him 'the staff of our hand.'
Convinced her son has died when he does not return on time, mourns and refuses to eat, watching the road daily.
Runs to embrace Tobias the moment she sees him returning.

funFacts: Her rebuke of Tobit over the disputed kid is one of the only moments in the book where his own righteousness is directly challenged by another character.

characters.name: Tobias

verses.note: Born to Tobit and Anna.
Sent by his father to find a poor kinsman for the feast; instead finds and reports a murdered Israelite in the marketplace.
Receives his father's complete farewell instructions and is told of the ten talents left with Gabael.
Sets out to find a travel companion and hires Azarias (Raphael in disguise) without recognizing him as an angel.
Nearly attacked by a great fish while washing in the Tigris; catches it on the angel's instruction and keeps its heart, liver, and gall.
Fears marrying Sara because her seven previous husbands all died on their wedding nights; is instructed how to survive the marriage.
Marries Sara at Raguel's house in Ecbatane, 'after the law of Moses.'
Prays alongside Sara on their wedding night instead of consummating out of lust, asking God to let them grow old together.
Anoints his father's eyes with the fish's gall, restoring Tobit's sight.
Inherits his father-in-law's and father's estates, lives to old age with honor, and dies at Ecbatane aged 127.

funFacts: Traveled with a dog that is mentioned twice as accompanying him (Tobit 5:16, 11:4), one of the few named animal companions across the indexed text so far.

characters.name: Achiacharus

verses.note: Appointed chief steward, cupbearer, and keeper of the signet under king Sarchedonus; uses his influence to bring Tobit safely home from hiding.
Supports and nourishes the now-blind Tobit until Tobit travels to Elymais.
Comes with his brother's son Nasbas to join in celebrating Tobias's safe return.
Cited by Tobit in his final testament as an example of how alms and righteousness deliver from death, having been nearly destroyed by Aman but saved.

funFacts: Identified in the text as Tobit's own nephew — 'my brother Anael's son.'

characters.name: Sara

verses.note: Reproached by her father's maids for the deaths of her seven husbands, each killed by the demon Asmodeus before the marriage was consummated.
Considers strangling herself rather than shame her aged father, then decides against it for his sake.
Prays toward her window instead, asking God either to let her die or to have mercy and end her reproach.
Her prayer and Tobit's are both heard together; Raphael is sent to heal them both and to give her to Tobias as his rightful kinsman.
Meets Tobias and Raphael as they arrive at her father's house.
Prays alongside Tobias on their wedding night rather than fearing another death.

funFacts: Her seven prior husbands are never individually named in the text.

characters.name: Raphael

verses.note: Found by Tobias as a hired travel companion; introduces himself under the disguised human name Azarias, son of Ananias the great.
Instructs Tobias to keep the fish's heart, liver, and gall after they catch it in the Tigris.
Instructs Tobias how to use the fish's smoke to drive off the demon Asmodeus on his wedding night.
The smoke he prescribed drives Asmodeus to 'the utmost parts of Egypt,' where Raphael binds him.
Tells Tobias in advance how the fish's gall will heal his father's blind eyes.
Reveals his true identity — 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints' — and explains he was sent in answer to Tobit's and Sara's prayers.
Vanishes from their sight immediately after the revelation.

funFacts: The name 'Azarias, son of Ananias the great' he gives in chapter 5 is his own cover story, not a real genealogy — his angelic nature is disclosed directly in 12:15.

characters.name: Raguel

verses.note: Welcomes Tobias and Raphael into his house, remarking how closely Tobias resembles his kinsman Tobit.
Agrees to give Sara to Tobias in marriage 'after the law of Moses,' despite the danger given her seven previous husbands' deaths, and writes a sealed marriage covenant.
Secretly digs a grave in the night, fearing Tobias has also died on the wedding night.
Praises God on learning both are alive, has the grave filled in, and keeps a fourteen-day wedding feast.
Gives Tobias and Sara half of his goods, servants, and cattle when they depart for Nineve.

funFacts: Digs his son-in-law's grave in secret before ever learning whether he actually needs it.

verses.note: Raguel's wife; present when he welcomes Tobias and Raphael.
Comforts her weeping daughter Sara before the wedding night, telling her to 'be of good comfort.'
Blesses Tobias as he departs, asking to live to see Sara's children before she dies.

characters.name: Asmodeus

verses.note: The evil spirit who has killed each of Sara's seven husbands before their marriages could be consummated.
Tobias fears the same fate awaits him because of this spirit's hold on Sara.
Driven off to 'the utmost parts of Egypt' by the smoke of the fish's heart and liver, then bound there by Raphael.

funFacts: The only named demon across the indexed text so far.

characters.name: Gabael

verses.note: Entrusted with ten talents of silver by Tobit at Rages in Media; described as 'the brother of Gabrias' — a different man from the like-named ancestor in Tobit's own genealogy at 1:1.
Tobit reminds Tobias of the deposit left in Gabael's keeping before giving his farewell instructions.
Raphael, disguised as Azarias, claims to know him personally as 'our brother Gabael.'
Raphael travels to Rages, delivers the handwriting bond, and receives the sealed bags of silver from him.

funFacts: Shares his name with an unrelated ancestor in Tobit's own genealogy (Tobit 1:1) — a real naming collision, not the same person.

verses.note: Succeeds his father Enemessar as king of the Assyrians.
In his wrath, slays many Israelites fleeing from Judea.
Seeks Tobit for execution after learning he secretly buried the slain.
Killed by two of his own sons, who then flee to the mountains of Ararat.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved background references, kept out of the character list above.

ancestorGabael.note: Tobit's own ancestor, 'son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael' — the same name as, but a different man from, the trustee Gabael of Rages (see naming-collision note in the book notes and on that character's funFacts).

enemessar.note: King of the Assyrians who first carried Tobit's tribe captive to Nineve, then favored Tobit as his purveyor. Father of Sennacherib. Not indexed as its own character — always background/passive in the text.

sarchedonus.note: Esarhaddon; succeeds his father Sennacherib and appoints Achiacharus as chief steward. Background monarch only.

sennacheribsSons.note: The two unnamed sons of Sennacherib who kill him and flee to the mountains of Ararat.

ananiasTheGreat.note: The father-name Raphael claims for his disguised identity, Azarias — part of the angel's cover story, not a real genealogical entry.

ananiasAndJonathas.note: Kinsmen of Tobit, 'sons of that great Samaias,' whom Tobit recalls worshipping alongside at Jerusalem — named only in passing to vouch for Azarias's claimed family.

nasbas.note: Achiacharus's brother's son, who comes with him to celebrate Tobias's return.

debora.note: Tobit's paternal grandmother, who raised and instructed him in almsgiving after he was orphaned by his father Tobiel.

sarasMaids.note: Her father's unnamed maidservants who reproach her for her seven husbands' deaths.

tobiasChildren.note: Tobit's dying charge is given to 'his son, and the sons of his son' — Tobias's own children are implied but never named within this book.
